\section*{Score-I papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P1-PHY-S2-Q02, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=numerical, subtopic={Bohr model}, answer={5.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S1 I0 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: Bohr model energy levels | steps: E = 13.6 Z\^{}2 (1/4 - 1/9) = 47.2 gives Z}]
A single electron orbits a stationary nucleus of charge $+Ze$, where $Z$ is a constant and $e$ is the magnitude of the electronic charge. It requires 47.2 eV to excite the electron from the second Bohr orbit to third Bohr orbit. Find the value of $Z$.
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=SI12-P1-PHY-S2-Q03, source={Score-I - Test 12 (09 Mar 2022)}, paper=1, qno=3, type=numerical, subtopic={Nuclear physics}, answer={4.00}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S1 I0 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: binding energy per nucleon curve | steps: read BE per nucleon for D, Li and He; Q = BE(products) - BE(reactants) and express in 5.5 MeV}]
The positions of ${}^2_1$D, ${}^4_2$He and ${}^7_3$Li are shown on the binding energy per nucleon curve as shown in figure. Find the energy released in the fusion reaction, ${}^2_1\text{D}+{}^7_3\text{Li}\to2\,{}^4_2\text{He}+{}^1_0\text{n}$ in multiple of 5.5 MeV.
\bfig{187.3}{SI12_p1_phy_s2_q03_1.png}
\end{bankq}

\section*{TOAS papers}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS18-P1-PHY-S1-Q01, source={TOAS - Test 18 (30 Oct 2022)}, paper=1, qno=1, type=multi, subtopic={Photoelectric effect}, answer={A,B,C,D}, answer_src=solved, working={Stopping potential 2 V and $\hbar\omega=6.26$ eV give $\phi=4.26$ eV; $I=\tfrac12\epsilon_0cE_0^2$ times $A\sin30^\circ$ gives $9.9\times10^{-4}$ W; yield $=(6\,\mu\mathrm A/e)/(P/\hbar\omega)=0.038$; saturation current $\propto E_0^2$ gives $6\times(25/15)^2=16.67\,\mu$A}, difficulty=8, diff_parts={K3 S3 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: photoelectric effect, intensity of an electromagnetic wave, quantum yield | steps: read the stopping potential and saturation current from the graph; work function from the photon energy; intensity from E0 and power on the tilted plate; yield from photon rate; scaling of saturation current}]
In given experiment on the photoelectric effect monochromatic plane wave of light falls on a metal plate of area 66.3 cm$^2$ at angle $30^\circ$ as shown. Electric field in light wave varies according to $E=E_0\cos(\omega t+\phi_0)$ where amplitude $E_0=15$ V/m, angular frequency is $\omega=9.5\times10^{15}$ rad/s. Dependence of photoelectric current $I$ on voltage applied $V$ between the electrodes is shown by graph. Select the correct statement (s).
\bfig{119.0}{TOAS18_p1_phy_s1_q01_1.png}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{Work function of metal plate is 4.26 eV.}
\opt{B}{Power received be metal plate by radiation is $9.9\times10^{-4}$ W.}
\opt{C}{Quantum yield (photoelectric efficiency) in the experiment is 0.038.}
\opt{D}{If amplitude of electric field in incident light is made 25 V/m then saturation current will become 16.67 $\mu$A.}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS18-P1-PHY-S1-Q02, source={TOAS - Test 18 (30 Oct 2022)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=multi, subtopic={de Broglie waves}, answer={A,B,C,D}, answer_src=solved, working={(A) same $m$ and $\lambda$ give same $p$ and KE; (B) equal and opposite momenta; (C) $p^2/2m=hc/\lambda$ gives $\lambda_{dB}=\sqrt{h\lambda/2mc}$; (D) $r=p/qB$ gives $r_p:r_\alpha=2:1$}, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K2 S2 I1 C0 F1}, diff_note={concepts: de Broglie wavelength, momentum and energy relations | steps: equal mass and wavelength; equal and opposite momenta in an explosion; energy absorbed by a free electron; radius ratio in a magnetic field}]
Select correct statement(s) :-
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{If two particle having same mass have same De-Broglie wavelength then they have same kinetic energy and same momentum.}
\opt{B}{When a bomb at rest explodes into two unequal pieces then both pieces have same De-Brogli wavelength.}
\opt{C}{When a photon of wavelength $\lambda$ incident on a free electron at rest then it's De-Broglie wavelength becomes $\sqrt{\dfrac{h\lambda}{2mC}}$, where $m$ is mass of electron.}
\opt{D}{A proton and an alpha particle are moving along circular path under same uniform magnetic field, then ratio of radius will be 2 : 1 if they have same De-Broglie wavelength}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS18-P1-PHY-S2-Q07, source={TOAS - Test 18 (30 Oct 2022)}, paper=1, qno=7, type=single, subtopic={Radioactivity}, answer={C}, answer_src=solved, working={Pu to U is alpha (T); $\mathrm{H^3\to He^3}$ is beta minus (R); $\mathrm{Pa^{230}\to Th^{230}}$ is beta plus (P); $\mathrm{I^{137}\to I^{136}}$ is neutron emission (S)}, difficulty=1, diff_parts={K1 S1 I0 C0 F0}, diff_note={concepts: types of nuclear decay | steps: compare mass and atomic numbers; assign each decay}]
Match list-I of nuclear process with list-II containing parent nucleus and one of end product of each process and then select the correct answer using codes given below the lists.
\begin{center}\footnotesize\setlength{\tabcolsep}{2pt}
\begin{tabular}{|L{0.8cm}L{1.6cm}|L{0.6cm}L{3.3cm}|}\hline
\multicolumn{2}{|c|}{List-I}&\multicolumn{2}{c|}{List-II}\\\hline
(I)&Alpha decay&(P)&${}_{91}\mathrm{Pa}^{230}\to{}_{90}\mathrm{Th}^{230}+\dots$\\\hline
(II)&$\beta^{\ominus}$ decay&(Q)&${}_{30}\mathrm{Zn}^{57}\to{}_{29}\mathrm{Cu}^{56}+\dots$\\\hline
(III)&$\beta^{\oplus}$ decay&(R)&${}_{1}\mathrm{H}^{3}\to{}_{2}\mathrm{He}^{3}+\dots$\\\hline
(IV)&neutron emission&(S)&${}_{53}\mathrm{I}^{137}\to{}_{53}\mathrm{I}^{136}+\dots$\\\hline
&&(T)&${}_{94}\mathrm{Pu}^{239}\to{}_{92}\mathrm{U}^{235}+\dots$\\\hline
\end{tabular}\end{center}
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{I $\to$ T;II $\to$ S;III $\to$ P;IV $\to$ R}
\opt{B}{I $\to$ T;II $\to$ P;III $\to$ Q;IV $\to$ S}
\opt{C}{I $\to$ T;II $\to$ R;III $\to$ P;IV $\to$ S}
\opt{D}{I $\to$ Q;II $\to$ R;III $\to$ S;IV $\to$ P}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS18-P1-PHY-S3-Q02, source={TOAS - Test 18 (30 Oct 2022)}, paper=1, qno=2, type=numerical, subtopic={Nuclear physics}, answer={0.62}, answer_src=solved, working={Non-relativistic positron momentum $pc=\sqrt{2\cdot0.5\cdot0.04}=0.2$ MeV; photons carry $1.04$ MeV in total with $E_1-E_2=pc=0.2$, so $E_1=0.62$ MeV}, difficulty=5, diff_parts={K1 S2 I1 C1 F1}, diff_note={concepts: annihilation with momentum conservation | steps: momentum of the positron; total energy; photon energy difference from momentum}]
A positron has 0.04 MeV kinetic energy. When it collide with an free electron at rest then they annihilate each other. One of the two photon produced is found to be moving in direction of incident positron. It's energy $x$ MeV. Find $x$. Neglect any relativistic effect. [mass of electron = mass of positron $=\left(\dfrac{0.5}{C^2}\right)$ MeV ]
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS18-P2-PHY-S1-Q01, source={TOAS - Test 18 (30 Oct 2022)}, paper=2, qno=1, type=single, subtopic={Bohr model}, answer={A}, answer_src=key, difficulty=2, diff_parts={K1 S1 I1 C0 F0}, diff_note={concepts: spectral frequencies at large n | steps: difference of reciprocal squares for n to n-1 and n to n-2; compare}]
In a hydrogen atom like spectrum if an electron de-excite from higher energy level ($n\gg1$) to a lower energy level then first few frequency of emitted light (Ex : $n$ to $n-1$ or $n$ to $n-2$) are nearly :
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{In Arthmetic progression}
\opt{B}{In Geometric progression}
\opt{C}{In Harmonic progression}
\opt{D}{In ratio $1^2:2^2:3^2$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
\begin{bankq}[id=TOAS18-P2-PHY-S1-Q03, source={TOAS - Test 18 (30 Oct 2022)}, paper=2, qno=3, type=single, subtopic={X-rays}, answer={B}, answer_src=key, difficulty=3, diff_parts={K2 S2 I0 C0 F0}, diff_note={concepts: photoelectric effect, X-ray cutoff | steps: maximum kinetic energy; cutoff condition; work function}]
A photon of wavelength $\lambda$ is incident on photoelectric plate \& most energetic electron from plate is now incident on target metal of x ray tube. If cut off wavelength of emitted photons from target material is $2\lambda$ then work function of photoelectric plate is :
\begin{qoptions}
\opt{A}{$\dfrac{hc}\lambda$}
\opt{B}{$\dfrac{hc}{2\lambda}$}
\opt{C}{$\dfrac{hc}{4\lambda}$}
\opt{D}{$\dfrac{hc}{8\lambda}$}
\end{qoptions}
\end{bankq}
